newsitem.title: FRANCE: French Communists consult Socialists on tactics.
newsitem.headline: French Communists consult Socialists on tactics.

text.p: French Communist leader Robert Hue said on Monday he could find common ground on Europe with the Socialists after the left upset the right in the first round of a parliamentary election.
He said contacts were under way between the two parties on how to fight next Sunday's run-off, but declined to say whether they could reach an agreement on a government programme.

Hue told France Inter radio the Communist Party, which polled nearly 10 percent of the votes, could win up to 30 seats in the National Assembly. The Socialists polled close to 24 percent and are tipped to win between 240 and 280.
"On the night of the run-off we will look into the conditions under which a majority and possibly a government agreement can emerge. We are not there yet," he said.
Hue, who unlike the Socialists opposes the Maastricht Treaty, said the Communists were not against Europe and were prepared to discuss new European policies.
"The Communist Party is not Europhobic. It is deeply in favour of another Europe. It does not stand for this liberal Europe which translates into austerity and thousands of redundancies," he said.

"The left can very well agree on the coherent axis of a European policy that will not be ultra-liberal. The Communist Party is positive about a Europe which would not be Maastricht's Europe," he said.
"If the left wins a majority it can open talks with its European partners on giving Europe a new orientation. Nothing is closed on that matter," he said.
